To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the (1,1)-EA is a very good algorithm for finding approximate solutions to vertex cover problems.

(a) for the worst case, the (1+ 1)-EA is a 1.999... approximation algorithm for vertex cover; (b) the algorithm is a polynomial time algorithm for vertex cover instances where the maximum vertex degree is at least three; (c) the algorithm is not a 1.00001 approximation algorithm for vertex covers of graphs where all vertex degrees are at least four.
the (1 + 1)-EA has an approximation ratio of at most two for vertex cover and that it can solve the problem efficiently when vertex degree is bounded by two.
In summary, our research is concerned with
worst case approximation analysis of the (1,1)-EA for the vertex cover problem.

EAs are not a panacea for the vertex cover problem.
the (1+(1)) EA cannot be used as a general purpose optimization algorithm for the vertex cover problem but it is efficient for certain subclasses of the problem.
